tracks.description: Track ids. Not an enum: content/curriculum/00-tracks.json is the one source of truth and validate.py checks every id against it (replan §1.8). The enum that used to live here drifted twice — it was missing rock-metal, jam and beautiful when P10 added a Chopin prelude to the Beautiful-pieces module.

levelSource.description: Whether `level` was decided for this piece or estimated — a whole opus banded to one number on import, or computed from features. The app prints an estimate as '≈ L7.1' and offers Re-level (replan §1.4).

compositionStatus.description: Whether the *composition* is public domain, as distinct from the edition's licence in `source.license` (`00` D23). A transcription may be CC0 while the song it transcribes is not. `unknown` is the honest answer for most of PDMX: the dataset says the upload is public domain and says nothing about the work. Items that are not `pd` are tagged `personal-build` and are placeholders in a strict-licence build.

targetSkills.description: What the item is chosen to train: skill ids from vocabulary v0 (content/curriculum/vocabulary/skills.json), the primary first. Declared, never evidence: a run is evidence of a skill only through a measurement (design 2026-09-26 §4). validate.py refuses an id the vocabulary lacks. C2 fills it on the nine sight-reading rows and D0 on the generated items whose family contract names a judged primary skill. Read at runtime only through app/src/curriculum/skillActivation.ts: the evidence readers act on the reading rows' alone, and selection acts on a declared skill only where eligibility.ts finds its opportunity established (E0).

demands.description: The material demands the build measured on the item's file with the app's own detectors (app/src/demands/detect.ts), in the vocabulary's order: demand ids from content/curriculum/vocabulary/demands.json. Measured, never declared (E0, build.attach_demands). The string "unmeasured" where a notated item could not be measured — the file would not load, it is not notation, or its notation is not bundled — with the reason in `measurement.reason`: never an empty list that reads as "no demands". Absent on a runtime drill, whose demands belong to each phrase it generates (`measurement.status` "runtime").

measurement.description: How the item's demands are known (E0): measured by the detectors (with the counts, the bars, steps and notes, and the demands provided at a useful density), unmeasured (with the reason), or made at runtime (with the reason). Written by build.attach_demands for a bundled item and by the import path for an imported score.

reason.description: Why the demands are unmeasured, or why a runtime drill has none of its own.

definitions.description: EVIDENCE_DEFINITIONS (app/src/evidence/evidence.ts) the demands were measured under.

detectors.description: The fingerprint of the files that decide a measurement (tools/content/demands.py DEFINITION_FILES).

located.description: Per demand, the number of places its detector located (only the demands located at least once).

established.description: The demands the item provides at a useful density (content/sources/opportunity-density.json, or a generated family's own contract density): the opportunities eligibility reads, told apart from incidental presence.

contract.description: Of `established`, the demands only the generated family's contract density establishes.

misread.description: Detector readings known to be wrong on this file, and why (the clef assumption: an upper staff written in the bass clef). They stay among the ids and never establish an opportunity.

provenance.description: Where the item came from and how each fact about it is known (E0; R35, R15, R11): the source kind, the edition, composition and arrangement identities, the converter or generator by version, each fact labelled measured, inferred, authored, reviewed, unmeasured or runtime, and R42's two review decisions as separate bits. Never flattened into one field.

quarryKeep.description: A PDMX row's quarry decision (`keep`): a source-level decision of the quarry, never either review bit (Part 12 §14). The reviewer's note stays in content/sources/pdmx.json: it is working prose with no source.

physical.description: A generated item's declared large-hand voicing, with its prerequisite and alternative (D0 finding 5).

review.description: R42's two decisions, apart: `score` a person judged the score usable and faithful; `teaching` a person judged it a good teaching use for its claimed role. null: no person has decided.

role.description: Relative to the primary target skill (design 2026-09-26 §7): the same notes every time, a new realisation of the same constraints, or a different surface for the same skill. Written on the generated items from their family contracts (D0); no selector reads it yet (D4 brings roles to selection).

notation.description: What the score file actually says, read from the MusicXML at build time by build.py's attach_notation and never from a title. Absent where the file could not be parsed. This exists because every other field describing a piece is asserted rather than measured - level is a constant or a regression, tracks came from the import bucket, genre from the id prefix - so choosing a song for a rung, or writing a sentence about one, had nothing but a name to go on.

bars.description: Counted inside one part. Counting across the document multiplies by the number of parts.

keys.description: Every key signature the score carries, in order. Two entries means it changes key.

times.description: Every time signature, as written, e.g. "3/4". A waltz says so here and nowhere else.

chordCount.description: How many chord symbols are printed. Zero means a rung about chord symbols cannot use this piece to teach them.

chords.description: The distinct chord symbols, capped at 24. This is what says whether a piece is I-IV-V or ii-V-I with sevenths.

swungMark.description: Whether a direction in the score says swing or shuffle.

finalBass.description: Pitch class (0-11, C=0) of the lowest note in the final measure. A fact about the file, not a claim about the key - but since <mode> is absent from 705 of 792 songs, a key signature alone cannot tell A minor from C major, and this is what distinguishes them. requires.mode stays strict and believes only an explicit tag; candidates.py uses this to widen a search. Null where the last measure has no pitched note.

file.description: path under content/ to .mxl/.musicxml, or to a .pdf that opens in the page viewer (04 §5b) rather than the Score screen; null for IMPORT or runtime-generated drills

variantOf.description: id of the parent song when this is simple/full/easy edition

kind.description: on a type=drill item this selects the runtime screen; on a type=exercise item it records what generated the notation and needs no screen (docs/05 §7)

help.description: kind: simon only (docs/04 §5c-2) — which rung of the help ladder the item opens on: keys lit and named as the chain plays, keys lit on a replay after a wrong note, or sound alone. The learner switches it on the card and the choice is then remembered per item.

alternatives.description: ids of other catalog items that train the same thing — what the app offers for "swap this", and what an import-only item points at so it is never a dead row (docs/00 D21, docs/04 §2). Every id must resolve; validate.py checks it.

sections.description: named practice sections (bar ranges) for the loop feature
